content.title: Project Hail Mary (2026) ⭐ 8.5 | Drama, Sci-Fi, Thriller
content.text: Videos21Featured reviewsHumanity needs this kind a moviesProject Hail Mary is the kind of movie that reminds you why you love cinema. It's been a long time since I felt such mixed emotions while watching a film-happiness, sadness, love, hope-everything is there. I went into it completely blind. I didn't watch a trailer; I only knew that Ryan Gosling was starring and that it was directed by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller, and that alone made me believe it would be something special.And it really was something special.The direction is fantastic, the visuals are beautiful, and the music is enormous-it melts perfectly into the writing and the story. Everything works together to create something warm, emotional, and incredibly human.At its heart, this is a movie about friendship, loneliness, change, evolution, bravery, and sacrifice. It's about doing good even when the situation feels impossible, and how goodness and courage can come back to you in unexpected ways.In a world that often feels dark and heavy, this film feels like a bright side. It brings genuine joy-the kind of joy movies are supposed to give you.An Epic Yet Intimate, moving and enduring Sci-Fi TriumphProject Hail Mary feels like an instant modern sci-fi classic. It's both epic and intimate-and that contrast is exactly what makes it so special.On one hand, it's epic in scope and ideas, delivering a visually stunning and thrilling story with a powerful message about cooperation. No matter how high the stakes, it reminds us that connection, empathy, and care for one another are what truly matter.On the other hand, it remains deeply intimate. Much of the film focuses on the relationship between two unforgettable characters, watching them learn, connect, and bond despite being completely different in every possible way-all while trying to save each other's worlds. That emotional core is what elevates the film beyond its premise.The science is impressive and will satisfy any sci-fi fan. While the premise of the film may not be entirely new, it feels fresh and original in execution. The atmosphere is outstanding, thanks to the cinematography, score, and remarkable visual effects.The script is exceptional, delivering a complete and satisfying arc for its characters. Yes, the film is long-but that length allows every moment to build toward a payoff that feels earned and deeply rewarding.The characters are the true highlight. Ryan Gosling delivers one of his most endearing performances, supported brilliantly by Sandra Hüller and James Ortiz. And of course, the direction by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller shines throughout-it truly feels like their film, blending science, humor, heart, and high-stakes storytelling into a seamless whole.Overall, this is a moving sci-fi epic that absolutely earns its place as a modern classic.Hollywood Debut of Academy Award Nominee Sandra HÜLLERSince STAR WARS (1977) and ALIEN (1979), so many science fiction films have graced the stage, and yet there's always a story that truly captivates and moves us. PROJECT HAIL MARY is a very positive surprise. And that's primarily due to the lead actors. Academy Award nominee Ryan Gosling plays a nerdy scientist who has to travel into space to find the first true friend of his life. And Academy Award nominee Sandra Hüller, in her first major Hollywood production (from Amazon MGM Studios), is captivating as an Angela Merkel-inspired super-organizer who, at the right moment, is prepared to force others to "make their happiness happen." And then there's this: Just like in TONI ERDMANN (2016), for which the exceptional actress received her first European Film Award, Sandra Hüller delivers a remarkable singing performance, becoming another magical moment in a film that is certainly not lacking in special moments.The story: Due to a loss of solar energy, Earth is on the brink of an ice age. In just a few years, millions of people will die. A molecular biologist (Ryan Gosling), who has always held a minority opinion, works as a substitute teacher and is recruited by an ESA employee (Sandra Hüller) for the Hail Mary project. The mystery of the energy loss is indeed uncovered. Only a dangerous space mission can save humanity. And so, against his express wishes, the molecular biologist finds himself aboard a spaceship. For him, this marks the beginning of a journey into the unknown, on which he will make many astonishing discoveries.Alongside world-renowned stars Ryan Gosling and Sandra Hüller, James Ortiz plays a crucial role as Rocky in this remarkable film. It takes some getting used to him and his character. But then something happens that underscores the film's unique magic. As a viewer, you allow yourself to connect with an utterly alien being and are richly rewarded.A magnificent film that celebrates the strength and fearless intelligence of nerdy outsiders! A truly excellent film!Touching, funny and captivating.Although the way this space adventure is written and filmed keeps you enraptured with the plot and sense of adventure, it is easy to forget that Ryan Gosling spends most of his time acting alone, and he deserves much credit for his seamless performance. Apparently, no green screen was used during the filming with a set built for the spaceship interior and an animatronic or puppet used for Rocky, with SFX added to enhance it afterwards.Based on Andy Weir's second novel, it has some similarities in structure to The Martian, in that a lone Spaceman must use science and his wits to save himself, and in this case, both humanity and his newfound friend, an Alien called Rocky. What is so enjoyable about this film is not the sense of looming disaster but rather the story about how two species meeting for the first time in the vastness of space learn to communicate, work together to solve the riddle of dying stars and to eventually become friends. It is a smart mix of tension and heartfelt adventure. It is the kind of film I can say is a departure from the formulaic expectations we might have from sci-fi disaster movies. So much is so good here that, for pure entertainment value, it is difficult to fault and I already want to watch it again.Sublime.I rarely write reviews on this site. But as this is an adaptation of one of my favorite novels of recent times, this was necessary.Being a Big fan of the novel (reading the book 3 times), and one of my favorite novels of all time, What can I say? A masterpiece of adaptation. With a talented screenwriter like Drew Goddard adapting the work and talented directors like Lord and Miller, I already imagined it would be at least great.Ryan Gosling was perfect in the role. This film will be nominated for several awards, it will be nominated for several Oscars, and Gosling will probably be nominated for best actor.Ther score of Daniel Pemberton (Spiderverse 1 2 3) is sublime, like a Vangelis score type, Greig Fraser (Dune parts 1 2) Cinematography it´s top notch, Charles Wood Design (from many MCU films) it´s out of this World. The effects are perfect, but for a certain character most of them (for the happyness of me and many fans ) they are made of practical effects and I always thought that was the right way to create them. Who read or watched the movie knows who I am talking about.Of course like in every adaptation, some things are removed, like some characters and scenes, but the main plot of course is here, and is faithful.This is a great year for sci-fi fans. Project Hail Mary adaptation, Disclosure Day from Spielberg (his return to directing aliens), Dune Part 3 from Villeneuve.I feel that Project Hail Mary will be one of the films with the most Oscar nominations in 2027, along with Christopher Nolan's Odyssey.
